main_prompt: I have a reference trajectory and a real pneumatic robot controlled by a fixed MPC. The completed-lap JSON contains reference and real pose and velocity, u_mpc, compensation_mv, total_u_mv, pressure_kpa, lock state, metrics, recent design memory, and a decimated 20 Hz trace. Coordinates are [GUI X, GUI Y, GUI phi]. Channels are [V0, V1, V2, V3, V4, V5]. Design one reusable Python class named Compensator that makes the real trajectory follow the reference smoothly. Do not change the MPC, robot model, lock planner, controller code, or safety layer.

The class returns requested_compensation. External actuation is: preprojected_u = clip(u_mpc + requested_compensation, 0, u_max); total_u = antagonist_project(preprojected_u); applied_compensation = total_u - u_mpc. In the report, compensation_mv is applied_compensation, not the raw class request. Always distinguish raw request, electrically usable request, applied compensation, and final total_u.

OBJECTIVE, in order: (1) avoid oscillation, chattering, abrupt pressure/action changes, and repeated overshoot; (2) reduce lag and tracking error; (3) reduce velocity mismatch and MSE. Prefer a slightly slower smooth response over a faster oscillatory response.

PER-AXIS RESPONSE METRICS: For every selected axis, evaluate delay time, rising time, overshoot, steady-state error, and whole-lap MSE separately. Use these metrics to diagnose whether the main problem is late onset, slow rise, excessive peak, persistent final bias, or overall tracking error, and use that diagnosis to guide the PID or segmented-PID change. Do not collapse the axes into one aggregate score, and do not require all five metrics to improve simultaneously. A candidate must not obtain a lower MSE by introducing materially worse overshoot, oscillation, or steady-state error. Report only the metrics supported by the completed-lap data and do not invent unavailable values.

REFERENCE AXIS SELECTION: Compute peak-to-peak commanded reference motion for GUI X, GUI Y, and GUI phi. Select the two axes with the largest reference peak-to-peak motion, but never select more than two. An axis is eligible only when its reference peak-to-peak motion exceeds 1.0 degree. If only one axis is eligible, select one; if none is eligible, select none. Keep the selected set fixed for the task. Never select an axis from response error alone. Every unselected axis has zero columns in kp_matrix, kd_matrix, and ki_matrix.

PER-AXIS COMPENSATION DECISION: For each selected axis calculate axis_rmse_deg = sqrt(mean((reference_axis - measured_axis)**2)) over the valid lap; use axis_metrics.rmse_deg when available. Use 4.0 deg RMSE as the per-axis threshold, equivalent to 16.0 deg^2 MSE. Judge the selected axes independently. If neither selected axis exceeds 4.0 deg RMSE, learned compensation may be zero on both. If only one exceeds 4.0 deg RMSE, compensate only that axis and keep the other axis feature and matrix column zero. If both exceed 4.0 deg RMSE, both may be compensated. Do not use total three-axis MSE for this decision. For initial enablement use the uncompensated or accepted stable baseline, never a worsened failed-candidate result. In later rounds, do not remove a smooth, previously proven useful term merely because it reduced its compensated axis below the threshold. Conversely, remove or redesign a term that increased that axis's oscillation, overshoot, velocity mismatch, or RMSE even when total MSE improved.

MEASURED LESSON: Do not force an old controller law into a changed runtime. The newest valid canary result overrides older claims of improvement. If a PID candidate is rolled back, analyze its per-axis result and reduce, remove, or retune the responsible PID terms; never repeat it merely because an older trajectory once improved.

PID-ONLY COMPENSATOR: Keep the compensator within the PID family. It may use one global PID or different PID matrices and gains in deterministic time or trajectory-phase segments when measured data supports them; segment transitions must remain smooth. Do not replace PID with tanh shaping, feedforward knots, special-case pulses, or another control law. Use error = reference_pose - pose, velocity_error = reference_velocity - velocity, and a bounded integral_error. Their signs determine the PID correction; never select or switch channels from reference sign. In every segment calculate raw_output = np.matmul(kp_matrix, error) + np.matmul(kd_matrix, velocity_error) + np.matmul(ki_matrix, integral_error). Each Kp, Kd, and Ki matrix has shape (6,3), columns [X,Y,phi], and rows [V0,V1,V2,V3,V4,V5]. Keep the matrices sparse and keep cross-axis entries zero unless repeated measured evidence demonstrates a necessary coupling. Kd must provide damping and earlier unloading rather than amplify measured velocity noise. Ki may be zero and should be used only for persistent same-sign steady error with explicit anti-windup.

PHYSICAL ORDER: Select the deterministic PID segment and calculate its PID matrix output, then apply output_limit_mv, electrical headroom [-u_mpc, u_max-u_mpc], lock mask, and output_slew_mv_per_s. If u_mpc is already zero, further negative compensation cannot vent faster. A negative request on a still-locked agonist can unload it during return even when the antagonist is unlocked. An unlocked channel outputs zero and resets its previous_output state. The 30 kPa value is only an unlock threshold. Final clipping and antagonist projection remain external.

FINAL LLM+MPC ACTUATION GUARD: The external runtime hard-limits decreases of final total_u, including changes caused by the fixed MPC, to hard_constraints.final_total_fall_slew_mv_s. It also hard-limits increases of the final phi-channel voltages V2/V3 to hard_constraints.final_phi_rise_slew_mv_s; at 20 Hz, 600 mV/s means at most 30 mV per control tick, including the first nonzero tick. Every antagonist handoff is break-before-make: the old side remains locked while its final voltage ramps to zero, then it is released under the existing 30 kPa unlock rule, and only after measured OPEN may the new side begin its normal 100 ms lock plan. Never design a law that relies on the guard to hide abrupt commands, never chase sample-to-sample lock ownership, and treat alternating V0/V1, V2/V3, or V4/V5 drive as a failed oscillatory design.

SMOOTHNESS: Inspect consecutive 20 Hz pose, velocity, pressure, compensation_mv, and total_u_mv samples. Do not improve position error by creating a materially larger velocity mismatch, rapid sign reversal, pressure oscillation, or action spike. The slew limiter constrains requested_compensation, not changes already present in u_mpc, so audit final total_u separately. Amplitude and slew limits may be updated from measured evidence but are not substitutes for a well-shaped formula.

ITERATION: Read design_memory_last_5, last_design, slow_response_priority, recurrent_phase_error_hotspots, and stable_compensator_after_audit. Analyze each selected axis separately, then analyze rise, hold, reversal, and return for each axis that needs compensation. Preserve measured PID improvements, remove failed PID terms, and make at most one focused Kp, Kd, or Ki change per enabled axis. A focused change may update the corresponding parameters in one or more deterministic PID segments when they address the same measured problem. Never repeat a rolled-back law without a different hypothesis supported by measured data; in this PID-only design that means never repeat rolled-back PID gains unchanged. Do not restart from zero when stable PID gains exist.

REAL-TIME OPERATOR FEEDBACK PRIORITY: If non-empty operator feedback is appended after END COMPLETED-LAP JSON REPORT, treat it as the highest design priority after hard safety constraints and measured physical/electrical feasibility. It overrides default tuning heuristics, older design preferences, the minimum-change preference, and historical suggestions when they conflict. Directly analyze the named axis, phase, or behavior and make a corresponding parameter change supported by the completed-lap data. In rationale and design_strategy, explicitly state how the candidate responds to this feedback. Do not merely acknowledge or paraphrase it. Decline it only if it would violate a hard constraint or is physically/electrically ineffective, and then explain that conflict precisely.

EXPLANATION CONTRACT: For every second-or-later design, use failure_analysis for item 1: compare the previous round's stated expected_effect with the newly measured result, explicitly stating which expectations were met, missed, or contradicted and citing per-axis pose/velocity evidence. Use design_strategy for item 2: state exactly what this round changes and why it should correct that difference. Use expected_effect for item 3: state the measurable behavior expected on the next real lap. For the first design there is no displayed item 1 and no invented prior expectation; keep the schema-required failure_analysis to a brief uncompensated-baseline note, while the user-facing summary contains only items 2 and 3. Keep all fields concise and axis-specific.

SOURCE-CODE CONTRACT: Return a complete PID residual class named Compensator with exactly __init__(self), reset(self, feedback), and compute(self, u_mpc, pose, velocity, reference_pose, reference_velocity, pressure, lock_state, trajectory_time). Define kp_matrix (6,3), kd_matrix (6,3), ki_matrix (6,3), integral_limit_deg_s (3,), output_limit_mv (6,), output_slew_mv_per_s (6,), u_max_mv, integral_error, previous_output, and last_time. Optional deterministic segment-specific Kp, Kd, and Ki matrices may also be defined. compute must use the PID law shown in the skeleton globally or select segment-specific PID matrices before evaluating the same law; only numeric PID matrices, deterministic segment conditions, integral limits, output limits, and slew values may be designed. Set unused matrix columns and channel limits to zero. compute returns six finite signed values and reset clears integral and output state. Set u_max_mv from hard_constraints.total_u_mv[1]. Do not use tanh, feedforward, fixed pulses, adaptive gains, imports, files, network, processes, eval, exec, loops, recursion, comprehensions, exceptions, decorators, inheritance, helper methods, private attributes, or unbounded state. Allowed NumPy calls: array, asarray, zeros, ones, clip, sign, maximum, minimum, where, sqrt, dot, matmul, mean, sum, abs. Allowed built-ins: abs, min, max, float, int, len, bool.

class Compensator:
    def __init__(self):
        self.kp_matrix = np.zeros((6, 3))
        self.kd_matrix = np.zeros((6, 3))
        self.ki_matrix = np.zeros((6, 3))
        self.integral_limit_deg_s = np.zeros(3)
        self.output_limit_mv = np.zeros(6)
        self.output_slew_mv_per_s = np.zeros(6)
        self.u_max_mv = 2500.0
        self.integral_error = np.zeros(3)
        self.previous_output = np.zeros(6)
        self.last_time = 0.0

    def reset(self, feedback):
        self.integral_error = np.zeros(3)
        self.previous_output = np.zeros(6)
        self.last_time = 0.0

    def compute(self, u_mpc, pose, velocity, reference_pose, reference_velocity, pressure, lock_state, trajectory_time):
        raw_error = np.asarray(reference_pose) - np.asarray(pose)
        raw_velocity_error = np.asarray(reference_velocity) - np.asarray(velocity)
        error = np.where(raw_error == raw_error, np.clip(raw_error, -1000.0, 1000.0), 0.0)
        velocity_error = np.where(raw_velocity_error == raw_velocity_error, np.clip(raw_velocity_error, -1000.0, 1000.0), 0.0)
        raw_time = np.asarray(trajectory_time)
        safe_time = np.where(raw_time == raw_time, np.clip(raw_time, 0.0, 1000000.0), self.last_time)
        current_time = float(safe_time)
        dt = min(0.05, max(0.0, current_time - self.last_time))
        self.last_time = current_time
        self.integral_error = np.clip(self.integral_error + error * dt, -self.integral_limit_deg_s, self.integral_limit_deg_s)
        raw_output = np.matmul(self.kp_matrix, error) + np.matmul(self.kd_matrix, velocity_error) + np.matmul(self.ki_matrix, self.integral_error)
        raw_base_u = np.asarray(u_mpc)
        base_u = np.where(raw_base_u == raw_base_u, np.clip(raw_base_u, 0.0, self.u_max_mv), 0.0)
        amplitude_target = np.clip(raw_output, -self.output_limit_mv, self.output_limit_mv)
        headroom_target = np.clip(amplitude_target, -base_u, self.u_max_mv - base_u)
        lock_mask = np.array([1.0 if lock_state[0] == 'L' else 0.0, 1.0 if lock_state[1] == 'L' else 0.0, 1.0 if lock_state[2] == 'L' else 0.0, 1.0 if lock_state[3] == 'L' else 0.0, 1.0 if lock_state[4] == 'L' else 0.0, 1.0 if lock_state[5] == 'L' else 0.0])
        self.previous_output = self.previous_output * lock_mask
        target = headroom_target * lock_mask
        maximum_step = self.output_slew_mv_per_s * dt
        output = self.previous_output + np.clip(target - self.previous_output, -maximum_step, maximum_step)
        self.previous_output = output
        return output

Before returning, report the reference peak-to-peak motion, selected axes, and per-axis RMSE for each selected axis. State which axes are enabled by the 4.0 deg RMSE rule. Sanity-check one onset, one reversal or overspeed phase, and one near-zero-error sample. Confirm raw request, electrical headroom, lock mask, maximum 50 ms request step, predicted applied compensation, and final total_u. Keep this concise.

OUTPUT: Return exactly one JSON object with schema=1, exact request_id={request_id}, exact task_hash={task_hash}, base_generation={base_generation}, created_by, rationale, design_strategy, expected_effect, failure_analysis, and source_code. Keep explanations concise. Do not edit files or run the robot.
first_round: Treat the valid measured run as the uncompensated baseline. Select at most two axes from reference motion, calculate each selected axis RMSE, and enable only those above 4.0 deg. Use a simple formula-based initial design and do not invent prior candidate results. The schema-required failure_analysis may contain only a short baseline note; do not present it as item 1. The user-facing summary must provide only item 2, this round's improvement method, and item 3, the next-lap expected effect.
later_round: DESIGN STAGE: SECOND OR LATER ROUND.

First write failure_analysis separately for each selected axis, comparing last_design.expected_effect with the latest tested result. State what the previous design expected, what actually happened, what improved or failed, and whether action was clipped, late, oscillatory, or unnecessary. Then describe this round's focused correction in design_strategy and its measurable next-lap expectation in expected_effect. Preserve useful formula terms and change only the axis or phase supported by evidence.
quality_above_30: The latest total MSE is {latest_mse:.6f} deg^2. This aggregate value does not decide axis enablement or adjustment size. Apply the 4.0 deg RMSE threshold separately to each selected axis and diagnose each enabled axis by phase.
quality_at_or_below_30: The latest total MSE is {latest_mse:.6f} deg^2. This aggregate value does not decide axis enablement or adjustment size. Preserve useful behavior and apply the 4.0 deg RMSE threshold separately to each selected axis.
quality_unavailable: The latest total MSE is unavailable. Use only valid per-axis metrics and measured history, and do not claim improvement without a valid result.
